neighbours.label: A quality criterion that is being prioritised or traded off ('in terms of sheer speed', 'quantity over quality', 'price-to-performance'), vs the same nouns used descriptively with no trade-off
fire: When it comes to sheer speed, no other train in Europe can match it.
Many shoppers now choose durability over price when buying furniture.
This laptop offers the best price-to-performance ratio in its class.
If your main priority is reliability, pick the older model.
The coach valued consistency over flashiness in every new player.
In terms of sheer volume, the harbour handles more cargo than any other.
The designers sacrificed comfort for weight savings on the racing bike.
For buyers who care most about simplicity, the basic phone is enough.
quiet: The speed of the train was recorded by the station's sensors.
The price of the furniture went up again after the new year.
This laptop has a bright screen and a small keyboard.
The reliability report was printed and handed out at the meeting.
The coach wrote the new players' names on the board.
The volume of the radio was turned down after midnight.
The designers painted the racing bike bright red for the show.
The basic phone comes in black or white and has a small screen.

predictions: Fire items 0.3-0.85 on the criterion noun or its modifier; descriptive uses under 0.1.
short: criterion being prioritised or traded off
notes: Card: ' growth' (emphasizing growth or value), ' sheer' (lethality), 'iciency' (power-efficiency), '-to' (performance-to-cost), ' overall', ' quantity' (instead of quality), '-round', 'ability' (manageability), Preis-'Le'istung.
